Coquitlam townhomes for sale: ground-level homes in strata buildings. The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® benchmark for townhomes in Coquitlam was $976,600 in September 2026 (-6.5% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Coquitlam townhomes sold, November 2025 to October 2026

307 townhomes sold in Coquitlam with a median price of $1,000,000 (the middle half sold between $871,500 and $1,199,500), taking a median of 17 days to sell at 98.5% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $638 per square foot, a median year built of 2020 and a median strata fee of $390 a month.

Coquitlam Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: This page covers townhomes across the whole City of Coquitlam, from Maillardville and Burquitlam in the west to Burke Mountain and Partington Creek in the northeast.

The townhouse stock clusters where the City has planned it: Burke Mountain under the Partington Creek Neighbourhood Plan, the City Centre and Burquitlam station areas, and infill sites rezoned to RT-2 Townhouse Residential across the older neighbourhoods.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Townhouses in Coquitlam are a multi-family form that needs a Form and Character Development Permit: the City requires that permit before subdividing, constructing or adding to a building in a Development Permit Area, covering design, landscaping, siting, parking and finishes.

The current building-permit list shows the form still being built at scale: a 142-unit, 3-storey townhouse project at 1395 Pollard Street on Burke Mountain, in 24 buildings, and 16 townhouses in 3 blocks at 3469 Baycrest Avenue, both with applications dated August 2026.

Older infill townhomes arrive one rezoning at a time: at 586 Thompson Avenue the City's notice proposed rezoning from RS-1 One-Family Residential to RT-2 Townhouse Residential for three 3-storey townhouse buildings holding nine units.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Townhouse zoning is RT-2 Townhouse Residential under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — the City's own land-sale document for 3596 Innes Court confirms that site is zoned RT-2 for townhouse development.

One zone is in flux: the City states the R-4 Intensive Small-Scale Residential zone will be reviewed as part of its upcoming Townhouse and Rowhouse Review, so R-4 townhouse-form rules may change — check current.
Creek-side townhouse sites can also sit in a Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area, where a permit is required before developing, subdividing, constructing or altering land.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The City sells townhouse land itself: its 2025 request for offers covered a 3.60-acre RT-2 townhouse site at 3596 Innes Court on Burke Mountain, bounded by Mitchell Street and Brownlee Avenue, beside a future park of about 2.0 acres.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: Coquitlam is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so a townhouse owner must complete the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Townhouse areas feed the Evergreen Extension: Coquitlam Central Station is the rail and bus hub for the Burke Mountain and City Centre clusters, connecting to the Millennium Line and the West Coast Express.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check creek proximity on any Burke Mountain or ravine-edge complex: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area layer shows where alteration needs a permit, and strata depreciation reports are where retaining walls and drainage show up for existing complexes.
Check the zoning in force at purchase, not at listing: the Townhouse and Rowhouse Review, including the R-4 zone, is an open City project, so townhouse-form rules are a check-current item.
